To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a large deletion in the genome of the magnetotactically competent strain MSR-1 of Magnetospirilium gryphiswaldens, which includes the mamAB and mamCD gene clusters, results in the loss of magnetosome crystals.

a large chromosomal deletion, which comprised the entire mamAB, mamDC clusters and further putative operon encoding a number of other magnetosome-associated protein, was identified in the nonmagnetic mutant strain MSR-1b.

we have identified a large deletion of the magnetosome island in a nonmagnetic mutant of Magnetospirllum gryphiswaldene, which comprises the entire mamAB cluster as well as the mamDC cluster and further putative operon encoding a number of other magnetosome associated proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of magnetotactic bacteria with special emphasis on the magnetosome membrane.
the characterization of the nonmagnetic mutant strain MSR-1b of Magnetospirillium gryphiswaldens and the identification of a large magnetosome island.
the characterization of a spontaneous nonmagnetic mutant of M. gryphiwaldense and the analysis of a putative magnetosome island.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mamAB and mamCD operons are not essential genes for the biosynthesis of magnetosome crystals and for their assembly within membrane vesicles in M. gyrphiswaldense.
the magnetosome island in Magnetospirillum is a large chromosomal island of approximately 80 kbp in size which is flanked by two insertion elements.

the magnetotactic bacteria are a group of organisms that have evolved the capacity to synthesize intracellular magnetic particles, the so-called magnetosomes, in order to navigate through their aquatic environment by means of magnetotaxis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetosome island in the MSR-1 strain of M. gryphyswaldense is a region of the genome that contains genes for magnetosome synthesis and is also involved with iron uptake and metabolism.
the deletion of a large region of the genome of M. gryphsiwaldense, which includes genes encoding magnetosome-associated proteins, results in a nonmagnetic phenotype.
we have isolated a nonmagnetic mutant of M. gryphsivaldense and identified a large chromosomal deletion which comprises a putative large island of magnetosome-associated genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetosome island is not only the site of genes encoding magnetosome-associated proteins but also harbors other magnetosome-specific genes.
the magnetosome island is a highly dynamic region in M. gysphiswaldense.
the magnetosome island in magnetotactic bacteria is a large chromosomal region, and the deletion of this region in the MSR-1B strain results in a loss of magnetosomes.
